subject: Streaming + Funcalls integration confirmation and next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Torres <elaine@lumera.ai>, Jake Perkins <jake@lumera.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-05T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up and integration confirmation

Hi Elaine / Jake,

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick post-call recap and where we landed from a product/engineering perspective so we have aligned next steps. Feel free to correct anything I mis-summarize.

Key pain & goals you highlighted:
- High variability on end-to-end latency for reranking calls during peak traffic (spikes to >1.2s per query right now).
- Embedding compute cost is a primary driver of monthly spend; want to batch/quantize and route lower-sensitivity traffic to cheaper variants.
- Need deterministic structured output for the triage UI (JSON with {category, priority, snippets}) and consistent function-call behavior for downstream systems.
- Desire streaming responses for the agent UI to improve perceived latency and allow partial rendering of results.

What Redwood proposed during the call:
- Use streaming generation + function calling to produce validated JSON outputs; we'll provide sample function schemas and guardrails.
- Enable hybrid routing: high-SLA traffic -> fp16/fast variant; background bulk embedding jobs -> quantized variant with batching.
- Prefix/KV caching and continuous batching for repeated/rerank queries to cut token cost.
- A short SDK change: a compact helper for client-side streaming + funcall plumbing (we can PR an example hooks file).

Attachments: I attached a high-level integration diagram to show the routing/batching boundaries and recommended SDK hook points.

Next steps / owners:
- Lumera: share a small sample of production queries (10–100 rows) and a rubric for what you consider acceptable JSON outputs (Elaine).
- Redwood: schedule a technical deep-dive (60–90m) to map the function schemas, streaming hooks, and batching profiles (Marcus).
- Redwood: produce an SDK proof-of-concept showing streaming+funcall wiring and an example rerank pipeline (Grace/Kim).

Proposed dates for deep-dive: Jan 11–13 (we suggested Jan 12 at 16:00 UTC in the calendar link below).

Thanks again — I'm optimistic there's a clear path to reduce your per-query cost while improving app responsiveness.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: lumera_arch_diagram.pdf (PDF)]
From: Elaine Torres <elaine@lumera.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-06T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up and integration confirmation

Hi Marcus — appreciate the clear recap. All looks right; a few clarifications and answers to your asks:

1) Sample data — attached are 50 representative queries and current rerank scores (anonymized). We marked which responses must contain structured fields vs. free-text for the UI.
2) Latency profile — spikes correlate with concurrent large batch jobs. If you can recommend a routing policy that keeps interactive traffic isolated from bulk jobs, that would help a lot.
3) Function schemas — we'll draft the minimal schema for category/priority/snippet and share before the deep-dive.

One note on security: we need confirmation that KV caching can be scoped per-customer and that embeddings don't leak across tenants. Can you confirm isolation model?

We can do the Jan 12 slot for the deep-dive. Thanks for the attachment — the diagram is helpful.

Best,
Elaine Torres
Head of Search & Relevance, Lumera AI
[Attachment: lumera_sample_queries.csv (CSV)]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-06T16:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Re: Intro + demo — follow-up and integration confirmation

Marcus — forwarding Elaine's note. Two internal items before the deep-dive:

1) Security answer: KV/prefix cache will be per-tenant namespaces; embeddings storage will use per-customer keys and AES256 encryption at rest. I'll pull the short security FAQ and SOC2 reference to confirm for Elaine.
2) Engineering ask: we should prepare two example routes for the deep-dive — (A) low-latency interactive path (streaming + fp16 model + function-call validation) and (B) low-cost batch path (quantized model + scheduled embedding jobs).

Grace — can you lead the SDK POC (streaming example + funcall schema) and have a changelist we can demo? Marcus, I'll add the security note and SOC2 link to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks,
Kimmy
